One ball. 15 seconds.

Keep the template camera and ports. Guide the chrome ball from entry to exit.

Get the starter file ↓
Challenge rules & technical settings
  • TimingFrames 0–449 at exactly 30 fps. Entry at frame 113; complete exit between 335 and 340.
  • Format1080 × 1920 portrait or higher, same aspect ratio. Deliver an H.264 or H.265 MP4.
  • Camera & boxKeep the 50 mm lens, preset camera animation, box dimensions and ports. Decorate the box; do not resize it.
  • The ballA 5 cm chrome ball enters with gravity. An identical ball leaves. Make forces and support believable.
  • PresentationNo titles, borders, camera shake or excessive filters. Sound design is welcome.
Motion blur: seconds versus Blender frames

The announcement specifies an exposure of 1/180 second. At 30 fps, Blender’s shutter duration is 30 ÷ 180 ≈ 0.167 frames. This is different from a 180° shutter (0.5 frames). Compare the supplied Motion Blur Reference image and test a moving frame.

Blender shutter units ↗

Rules: original announcement, 1:20–3:12 ↗. Timing, camera and resolution also checked in the supplied v1.4 Blender template.

Before editing the old Blender template

The source file contains a baked rigid-body cache. Clear it before changing the simulation, then replay from its start and rebake. Do not assume an old bake will reproduce correctly in a newer Blender version. Preserve the Camera action. The original readme’s submission link and deadline belong to 2021.

These studies use different teaching scales and camera setups. The challenge ball is 0.05 m. Measure and fit any reused mechanism to the original template, apply scale, then recheck collisions, margins and timing. Keep the challenge camera and frame range unchanged.

02 / THE ANIMATION TOOLKIT

Explore the techniques.

Pick a technique. Watch, open the Blender file, then try one change.

01 / 25 min · hands-on

One slat. An endless spiral.

A rotating Array and a traveling camera create the illusion of a sphere rolling along an endless spiral.

Looping preview

Download Array loop ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Make the slats thinner without changing the loop.

Reveal a solution

Edit the source slat thickness in Edit Mode. Keep the offset Empty, repeat spacing and travel keys unchanged; play a complete loop to check the seam.

Build it step by step

Inspect: SLAT → Array · ARRAY OFFSET → transforms · SPIN / LOOP TRAVEL → animation

  1. Start with one thin rectangular slat. Apply Scale, then add Bevel before Array.
  2. Inspect ARRAY OFFSET: Y spacing is 10 ÷ 23; each copy turns −180° ÷ 23 around Y. This file uses the Empty-driven Array interface for the same repeating twist.
  3. SPIN turns the source and its offset 360° over frames 0–120. LOOP TRAVEL moves the camera, sphere and lights 20 units along Y.
  4. The sphere rotates −1080° around X. Its colored seam makes the spin visible. Keep interpolation Linear for all three motions.
  5. Render frames 1–120. Frame 0 is the matching boundary pose; including both 0 and 120 would duplicate it.
Use it in your machine

Use repeated geometry and synchronized phases for conveyors and kinetic sculptures. Keep the challenge camera unchanged; animate the mechanism instead of copying this study’s traveling camera.

When it does not work

This is a coordinated visual illusion, not a rigid-body simulation. Changing spacing, phase or travel independently can break contact and the loop. The tutorial’s newer Array controls correspond here to the offset Empty’s translation and rotation.

02 / 25 min · hands-on

Move on a path—or bend around it.

The reference bends a ribbon using modifiers. Compare that with a real Follow Path constraint, which moves an object without bending it.

Preview · replay to restart

Download Paths & constraints ↓Companion: Follow Path constraint ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Move the carrier to the middle of its route.

Reveal a solution

Open the Follow Path companion. Enable Fixed Position and set Offset Factor to 0.5. Insert a key if you want to save this position in the animation.

Build it step by step

Inspect: RIBBON → Stretch / Twist / Curve · companion CARRIER → Follow Path

  1. Build an open path from a circle and two tangent semicircles. Merge joined points; leave the path endpoints open.
  2. Give a rectangular strip many lengthwise cuts. Align the strip and curve origins so deformation is predictable.
  3. Inspect the stack: Stretch → Twist → Curve → Bevel. This recreation uses local X; the tutorial uses −Y.
  4. Animate X Location to move the ribbon through the curve. Animate Stretch and Twist to reshape it as it approaches the circle.
  5. Open the companion Follow Path file. Fixed Position exposes Offset Factor: 0 starts the route; 1 finishes it. Follow Curve aligns the rigid carrier to the tangent.
Use it in your machine

Use the modifier for flexible belts or ribbons; use the constraint for guided carriers and lifts. A path does not automatically add gravity or rolling.

When it does not work

A Curve modifier deforms mesh vertices; a Follow Path constraint transforms the object. Apply scale, check the local deformation axis, and inspect accidental overlapping curve points if the ribbon folds incorrectly.

03 / 20 min · hands-on

A membrane that catches the impact.

A gold ball presses into an iridescent membrane. A single shape key controls the depression and folds inside the racket.

Looping preview

Download Shape keys ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Reduce the membrane deformation by half.

Reveal a solution

On the Impact shape key, halve the peak value at frame 40. Move the ball’s contact pose upward to meet the shallower membrane; scrub frames 25–55 to check contact.

Build it step by step

Inspect: MEMBRANE → Object Data Properties → Shape Keys → Impact

  1. Finish the membrane’s quad topology first. Keep its boundary fitted inside the oval rim.
  2. Add Basis, then Impact. Deform the middle down while leaving the edge fixed. The tutorial sculpts Cloth-brush folds; this file supplies editable radial folds.
  3. Set Impact to 1 when inspecting or sculpting the deformed shape. Value 0 restores the flat Basis.
  4. Key Impact at frame 25 = 0, 40 = 1, and 55 = 0. Match the ball’s height to the membrane during contact.
  5. Play the whole bounce. Inspect the lowest pose and the release before changing the frame or membrane materials.
Use it in your machine

Use this for flexible catches, diaphragms or soft launchers. Preserve the challenge ball’s size and deform the receiving object.

When it does not work

Shape keys blend vertex positions, so do not add or delete vertices after creating them. This is keyed deformation, not a cloth collision. If you change the depression depth, adjust the ball too.

04 / 25 min · hands-on

One impact starts the chain.

Seventeen separate dominoes transfer an impact through a real simulation. Marble, polished metal and studio lighting make the contact and reflections readable.

Preview · replay to restart

Download Rigid bodies ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Make the domino chain stop halfway.

Reveal a solution

Free the rigid-body bake, move one middle domino far enough away to break contact, then simulate from the start and rebake. Resetting the cache is essential.

Build it step by step

Inspect: DOMINO objects → Physics · Scene → Rigid Body World → Cache

  1. Scale and bevel one domino; apply Scale. Duplicate it into separate objects with regular gaps.
  2. Use Active rigid bodies on the dominoes and a Passive rigid body on the platform. These rectangular objects use Box collisions.
  3. Tilt the first domino beyond its support footprint. Merely shifting an upright block sideways will not reliably start a fall.
  4. Play from frame 1. Adjust spacing, friction and margins before making the simulation more complex.
  5. Bake when it works. The example already has a baked cache: Free/Delete Bake before editing, then rebake and reopen to verify playback.
Use it in your machine

Use short chain reactions inside your machine. Bake and check the required exit timing; simulation does not guarantee that a ball reaches the port on time.

When it does not work

A single Array object is not a set of independently simulated dominoes. Use separate objects. Stale caches ignore edits; large margins and unapplied scale can cause hovering or unstable collisions.

05 / 20 min · guided demo

Let the floor respond to the ball.

A moving controller lifts nearby tiles and changes their color. No individual tile needs keyframes.

Looping preview

Download Geometry Nodes ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Make the raised region narrower.

Reveal a solution

In the Map Range node, reduce the outer distance while keeping it above the inner distance. The proximity influence reaches zero sooner; the lift height can stay unchanged.

Build it step by step

Inspect: FLOOR → Geometry Nodes · PROXIMITY Empty → Location

  1. Grid → Mesh to Points (Faces) supplies a regular field. Instance a beveled tile onto those points.
  2. Object Info reads the controller’s relative Location. Feed it into Mesh Line’s Start Location with Count = 1.
  3. Geometry Proximity in Points mode measures distance to that point. Map Range turns distance into a clamped influence.
  4. Combine XYZ sends influence to Z; Set Position lifts the points before instancing. From Min makes the plateau; From Max controls the radius.
  5. Store the influence attribute for the tile shader. This adaptation realizes the instances so an ordinary shader Attribute node can read it. Move the Empty and watch height and color respond together.
Use it in your machine

Use reactive floors and mechanisms without hand-keying every part. Keep this a guided introduction today; students only need to edit the exposed values, not rebuild the full graph.

When it does not work

Use relative coordinates when controller and geometry live in different spaces. An Empty has no mesh: the one-point Mesh Line provides geometry for Proximity. The supplied node graph reads left to right.

06 / Optional · 20–30 min after class

Leave a trail that slowly recovers.

Orbiting sphere brushes displace a dense canvas. The grooves fade as the surface recovers.

Looping preview

Download Dynamic Paint · optional ↓
Watch the original tutorial
TRY IT

Make the trail disappear sooner.

Reveal a solution

Reduce the canvas Dissolve time, free the old cache and rebake the full warm-up range. Compare the same frame before and after.

Build it step by step

Inspect: CANVAS → Dynamic Paint · BRUSH objects → Dynamic Paint Brush

  1. Use a dense subdivided plane. Add Dynamic Paint as a Canvas and choose Displace.
  2. Give the spheres Brush settings and animate repeating 120-frame circular routes.
  3. Enable dissolve to recover the surface. This adaptation uses a 100-frame linear recovery so old laps clear before the next orbit.
  4. Bake frames 1–360, including warm-up. Render only frames 241–360, then inspect the boundary for a visible reset.
  5. Keep Smooth after Dynamic Paint. The download ZIP includes the external cache: extract the whole folder beside the .blend.
Use it in your machine

Optional exploration for grooves, imprints and recovering surfaces. It is outside the three-hour core workshop.

When it does not work

A plane with four vertices cannot hold a detailed groove. Changes to topology, brush motion or dissolve require a new bake. A repeating brush path alone does not guarantee a repeating simulation.

03 / DESIGN YOUR HAND-OFF

Build your machine.

Receive → transform the motion → release. Make the ball readable from the supplied camera.

Use two techniques. Create three events.

Receive → main event → release.

Exercise steps
  1. Open a copy of the original template. Keep its camera and frame range.
  2. Sketch three events in camera view. Work with simple cubes, curves and cylinders.
  3. Place timing markers between entry 113 and exit 335–340. Reserve the final release first.
  4. Make a low-resolution preview. Ask a partner to follow the ball without an explanation.
  5. Save the blockout and this plan. On Day 3, develop your own machine and refine its motion, materials and lighting.
PAIR REVIEW · 5 MIN

Can you see the ball? Does one event cause the next? Does each speed change have a reason? Is the exit on time?

Example timing plan—not a prescribed design

113–150: receive and guide. 150–235: one main mechanical event. 235–315: transfer toward the exit. 315–338: final release. These are planning windows, not instructions to hold the ball still at every boundary.

Submission checklist & export help

Preflight checklist

Class delivery package

  • Preview / final MP4450 frames, 30 fps, portrait. Play the exported file all the way through.
  • Editable .blendUse File → External Data → Pack Resources. Include any external simulation caches if used.

Suggested names: surname_machine_v01.blend and surname_machine_final.mp4.

Follow your instructor’s class deadline and upload location. This page does not submit files to the original competition.
A reliable rendering workflow

Render a low-resolution preview first. For final output, render frames 0–449 as a PNG sequence, then encode an MP4 at 30 fps. A sequence lets you resume a failed render without losing completed frames. Estimate render time from several representative frames.

What we review together

Clarity of the ball’s route, believable timing and forces, a distinct idea, a coherent visual style, and compatibility with the shared template. Fix contact and timing before decoration.
